mainTopic: Hearing your own words and saying them clearly in קריאת שמע, with related teachings on תחיית המתים and writing מזוזה
overview: This עמוד first asks whether the משנה that disqualifies a חרש from reading the מגילה follows רבי יוסי or רבי יהודה. After several challenges, the גמרא shows that the whole משנה can follow רבי יהודה if there are two kinds of קטן. Two ברייתות then seem to fit neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי. The גמרא solves this in two ways: one ברייתא is רבי יהודה's own view and the other is his teacher רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's, or the two are רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר. רב חסדא rules that you should hear your own קריאת שמע from the start, but it counts after the fact if you did not. רב יוסף limits the argument to קריאת שמע, and רבי טבי rules leniently in both disputes of the משנה. The עמוד then turns to related teachings: the grave gives back the dead like a womb (a source for תחיית המתים), even the commands are written in a מזוזה, and words that run together in שמע must be separated. Saying שמע carefully cools גיהנם. A new teaching of רבי חמא ברבי חנינא begins and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה could follow רבי יהודה. On that reading, a חרש should not read in the first place, but if he already read, it counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה follows רבי יהודה. Then it only means a חרש should not read in the first place, but if he already read, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that the משנה must follow רבי יוסי. It suggests a different reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier claim was that a חרש's reading is invalid even after the fact. That would fit only רבי יוסי. Here the גמרא says the word "except" might only mean לכתחילה, which would let the משנה fit רבי יהודה, who holds that not hearing your own reading is still valid בדיעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; it could be that
In the first place; the ideal way to act before doing it
After the fact; once it has already been done
It is fine; it is valid

steps.confusionAlert: Remember that the argument between רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה is only about after the fact. Both agree that in the first place you should hear what you are saying.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: The "it" is the משנה about reading the מגילה, which lists a חרש among those who may not read.

phrases.english: and it is only in the first place that he may not,
but after the fact, it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim (from the previous section) that the משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה in מגילה must follow רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's ban on a חרש could mean only לכתחילה. That reading fits רבי יהודה, so the משנה is no proof that a חרש's reading fails even בדיעבד.

steps.title: The חרש is grouped with the שוטה and קטן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The חרש is listed together with a שוטה and a קטן, whose reading never counts, so his reading doesn't count either, even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: That can't be. The משנה lists the חרש together with a שוטה and a קטן. Their reading doesn't count even after the fact, so a חרש's reading doesn't count even after the fact either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and defends the original claim. It uses the fact that the חרש appears in the same list as the שוטה and קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוטה and a קטן are not obligated at all, so their reading is useless even בדיעבד. If the חרש is placed alongside them, the משנה must mean his reading is also useless בדיעבד. That fits רבי יוסי, not רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is impossible
Similar to; in the same way as
A deaf person
A person without sound mind
A minor

phrases.english: This cannot enter your mind,
for it teaches a deaf person in the same way as an imbecile and a minor.

phrases.aramaic: מָה שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא —
phrases.english: Just as for an imbecile and a minor, even after the fact it does not count,
so too for a deaf person, even after the fact it does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 1 and defends the reading that follows רבי יוסי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from how the משנה is worded (the three cases are listed together)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on a חרש might be only לכתחילה, following רבי יהודה
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the חרש is grouped with the שוטה and קטן, his reading is invalid even בדיעבד

steps.title: Being listed together doesn't prove the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Each case in the list may have its own rule, even though they appear side by side.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps this one is as it is, and that one is as it is. Each case keeps its own rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 2. It argues that being listed together does not mean the cases are identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה may group the three only because none of them should read לכתחילה. The שוטה and קטן could be invalid even בדיעבד, while the חרש is invalid only לכתחילה. So the possibility that the משנה follows רבי יהודה is open again.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is; according to its own rule

phrases.english: And perhaps this one is as it is,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the שוטה and קטן, invalid even after the fact. "That one" is the חרש, invalid only in the first place.

phrases.english: and that one is as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the shared list. It does not prove that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Appearing in the same list does not force identical rules. Each case can keep its own level of invalidity.

steps.title: The last clause shows the opening is not רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new objection. The משנה ends with "רבי יהודה permits a minor," which implies the first part of the משנה is not רבי יהודה's opinion at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say the first part follows רבי יהודה? The last clause says "רבי יהודה permits a minor." That shows the first part is not רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא comes at the question from a different angle. It challenges the idea from step 1 that the opening of the משנה could follow רבי יהודה. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה names רבי יהודה disagreeing in its last clause, the unnamed opening is usually someone else's view. If so, the opening cannot be explained as רבי יהודה's soft (לכתחילה only) position. That brings back the view that it follows רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you explain it as following (a certain opinion)
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The opening clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Permits; rules valid
By implication; this shows that

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses a common method of reading a משנה: a named dissent in the סיפא usually means the רישא follows a different תנא. You will see this method in many places in the גמרא.

phrases.english: And can you really explain it as following Rabbi Yehuda?
But from the fact that the last clause teaches:
"Rabbi Yehuda permits a minor,"

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא לָאו רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא?!
phrases.english: this shows that the opening is not Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 reopened the idea that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, this step attacks that idea from a new angle
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in step 1 that the opening of the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא names רבי יהודה as disagreeing about a minor. This implies the רישא is a different תנא, so the רישא cannot be explained as רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: The whole משנה can be רבי יהודה, with two kinds of minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the entire משנה follows רבי יהודה. The משנה is missing words: the קטן who is disqualified is one who has not reached the age of חינוך, while a קטן who has reached חינוך is fit even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the whole משנה is רבי יהודה, and there are two types of minors. The משנה is missing words, and it really means: All are fit to read the מגילה except a deaf person, a שוטה and a minor. When is that said? About a minor who has not reached the age of training. But a minor who has reached the age of training is fit even from the start. These are רבי יהודה's words, since רבי יהודה deems a minor fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 4 by showing that the end of the משנה can belong to רבי יהודה too. The ending does not have to be a separate opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 argued that 'רבי יהודה permits a minor' means the first part is not his. The answer: the first part is speaking about a young קטן, and the ending explains that an older קטן (one who has reached חינוך) is fit. So the ending explains the first part rather than arguing with it, and the whole משנה stays with רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And perhaps; introduces another possible way to read things
Two types
The text is missing words; the גמרא fills in what it really means
Reached the age of training in מצוות
Deems fit / valid

steps.confusionAlert: 'Missing words' does not mean the משנה has a mistake. The גמרא is showing a fuller way to read the משנה so that its first part and its ending fit together.

phrases.english: And perhaps the whole [משנה] is רבי יהודה
and there are two types of minor
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
All are fit to read the מגילה
except a deaf person, a שוטה, and a minor.
In what case are these words said?
About a minor who has not reached the age of training
but a minor who has reached the age of training
is fit even from the start
these are the words of רבי יהודה
for רבי יהודה deems a minor fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the step 4 challenge by reading the משנה's ending as an explanation, not a disagreement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads missing words into the משנה (חסורי מחסרא) and splits the case into two kinds of קטן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ending 'רבי יהודה permits a minor' shows that the first part of the משנה is someone else's opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first part is about a young קטן, and the ending is about an older קטן. Both parts are רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A ברייתא lets a deaf person separate תרומה from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the conclusion that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who accepts an inaudible act only after the fact. It brings a ברייתא that lets a deaf person who speaks separate תרומה even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the משנה? Like רבי יהודה, that after the fact it counts, but not from the start? Then what about the ברייתא taught by רבי יהודה, the son of רבי שמעון בן פזי: A deaf person who speaks but does not hear may separate תרומה from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new problem. It brings a ברייתא that does not seem to fit the view we just gave רבי יהודה, and the next step shows exactly why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have just said that רבי יהודה holds that not hearing your own words is acceptable only after the fact. This ברייתא lets a deaf person act from the start, which goes further than that. The גמרא is preparing to ask whose opinion this ברייתא could be.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you set it up? With whose opinion did you explain it?
After the fact
Separates תרומה, the portion of produce given to a כהן
A deaf person who can speak but cannot hear

phrases.english: How did you explain it? Like רבי יהודה
that after the fact yes, from the start no?
But then that which רבי יהודה taught,
the son of רבי שמעון בן פזי:
phrases.notes: This is a different רבי יהודה, not the תנא whose opinion we have been discussing.

phrases.english: A deaf person who speaks but does not hear
may separate תרומה from the start,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the משנה is רבי יהודה, then brings a ברייתא that seems to go beyond his view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that רבי יהודה accepts an act done without hearing oneself only after the fact.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows a deaf person to act from the start, which seems to fit no known opinion. The next step completes the attack.

steps.title: The תרומה ברייתא fits neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ברייתא is. It cannot be רבי יהודה, who allows this only after the fact, or רבי יוסי, who never allows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is it? Not רבי יהודה and not רבי יוסי. If it is רבי יהודה, he says after the fact yes, from the start no. If it is רבי יוסי, he says even after the fact it does not count!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it set up. The ברייתא about the deaf person does not match either side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There seem to be only two opinions: רבי יוסי says not hearing yourself never counts, and רבי יהודה says it counts only after the fact. A ruling that allows it from the start fits neither one. So the ברייתא seems to have no author.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is it?
The תנא who holds that an inaudible recitation does not count, even after the fact

phrases.english: Whose opinion is it?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: Not רבי יהודה and not רבי יוסי.
If it is רבי יהודה,
after the fact yes, from the start no.
If it is רבי יוסי,
even after the fact, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 6 by showing that both possible authors are ruled out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי, read together with the view that רבי יהודה allows this only after the fact.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Allowing it from the start is more lenient than both known opinions. That leaves the ברייתא with no author.

steps.title: If רבי יהודה allows it from the start, whose is the ברכת המזון ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that רבי יהודה allows an inaudible act even from the start. A ברייתא says one should not say ברכת המזון silently, but if he did, it counts. That fits 'after the fact only', so whose opinion would it be?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what, does רבי יהודה allow it even from the start? Then what about the ברייתא: A person should not say ברכת המזון in his heart, but if he did, he has fulfilled his obligation. Whose opinion is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the problem around. Saying רבי יהודה allows this from the start only creates a new difficulty with another ברייתא. Step 9 spells out the difficulty, and Step 10 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To solve step 7, one might say רבי יהודה allows not hearing yourself even from the start. But then the ברכת המזון ברייתא, which allows it only after the fact, loses its author, since רבי יוסי does not accept it even after the fact. Each way of reading רבי יהודה fits one ברייתא and leaves the other without an author.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what? Tests the other option and shows it also has a problem
In his heart; silently, without saying the words out loud
He has fulfilled his obligation

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the real puzzle: two ברייתות seem to need two different views from רבי יהודה. The answer will need to explain how both can fit.

phrases.english: But rather, what? It is רבי יהודה,
and it is allowed even from the start too?
But then that which was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְבָרֵךְ אָדָם בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן בְּלִבּוֹ
phrases.english: A person should not say ברכת המזון in his heart
and if he did say it that way, he has fulfilled his obligation
whose opinion is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וַאֲפִילּוּ לְכַתְּחִלָּה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the other way to solve step 7 and shows that it creates a matching problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יהודה allows an inaudible act even from the start.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה allows it from the start, the ברכת המזון ruling ('not from the start, but valid after the fact') fits neither him nor רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The silent-blessing ברייתא fits no one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that says not to say ברכת המזון silently, but that it counts if one did, cannot be רבי יהודה's or רבי יוסי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי. If it is רבי יהודה, didn't he say it is allowed even from the start? And if it is רבי יוסי, didn't he say it does not count even after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question from Step 8. The ברייתא about saying ברכת המזון silently seems to match neither of the two known opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא takes a middle position: don't do it from the start, but it counts after the fact. Step 8 just suggested that רבי יהודה allows it even from the start, which is too lenient for this ברייתא. רבי יוסי says it never counts, which is too strict. So there seems to be no one left who holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; the right way to act before doing it
After the fact; once it has already been done
If (used to test each option one at a time)

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: Neither Rabbi Yehuda nor Rabbi Yosei.
If it is Rabbi Yehuda,
didn't he say it is fine even from the start?
phrases.notes: This is the idea from Step 8: that רבי יהודה allows an unheard recital even from the start.

phrases.english: And if it is Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא!
phrases.english: didn't he say it does not count even after the fact!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in Step 8 by ruling out both possible authors.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא about saying ברכת המזון silently
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Its middle position, only after the fact, matches neither רבי יהודה (from the start) nor רבי יוסי (never).

steps.title: One view is רבי יהודה's own, the other is his teacher's
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה himself allows it even from the start. The 'after the fact only' ברייתא reflects his teacher's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is רבי יהודה, and he allows it even from the start. And it is not difficult: this one is his own view, and that one is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both ברייתות can be linked to רבי יהודה. One gives his own opinion, and the other gives the opinion of his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא letting a חרש separate תרומה from the start is רבי יהודה's own view. The ברייתא allowing ברכת המזון only after the fact is his teacher's view. So the ברייתות do not contradict each other. Each reports a different person.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (the גמרא keeps its original claim)
And it is not difficult
His own (opinion)
His teacher's (opinion)

phrases.english: Really, it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and he allows it even from the start.
And it is not difficult:
this one is his own view,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ברייתא about the חרש separating תרומה from the start.

phrases.english: that one is his teacher's view.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the ברכת המזון ברייתא: not from the start, but it counts after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9 by splitting the two ברייתות between רבי יהודה and his teacher.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different person (רבי יהודה himself vs. his teacher)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות must reflect one person's view, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תרומה ברייתא is רבי יהודה's own view (allowed from the start). The ברכת המזון ברייתא is his teacher's view (only after the fact).

steps.title: Proof that רבי יהודה's teacher requires hearing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה reported his teacher רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view that שמע must be heard by one's own ears. רבי מאיר disagrees, saying intention of the heart is what matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יהודה said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: One who reads שמע must make it heard to his own ears, as it says 'Hear, Israel.' רבי מאיר said to him: But it says 'which I command you this day, upon your heart.' The words follow the intention of the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה's teacher held a stricter view. That view requires saying שמע loud enough to hear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reads the word 'שמע' (hear) as a requirement to hear yourself. That is the 'not from the start' view. רבי מאיר reads 'upon your heart' as saying the heart's intention is what counts, so hearing is not needed at all. This sets up the next answer.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
In the name of
That he make it heard to his own ears
The intention of the heart

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
One who recites Shema
must make it heard to his own ears,
as it is said: "Hear, Israel."
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said to him:
But it says:
"Which I command you this day, upon your heart,"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:6

phrases.english: after the intention of the heart
that is what the words follow.
phrases.notes: He means the words count based on what you mean in your heart, even if you don't hear them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 10's claim that רבי יהודה's teacher held a different, stricter view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's teacher, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, requires שמע to be heard by one's own ears
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, with רבי מאיר's response

steps.title: A second answer: רבי יהודה versus רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Now that רבי מאיר's view is known, רבי יהודה can hold like his teacher. The lenient תרומה ברייתא then belongs to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, you can even say that רבי יהודה holds like his teacher, and it is still not difficult: this one is רבי יהודה, and that one is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the full ברייתא to give a second way to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher: only after the fact. So the ברכת המזון ברייתא is רבי יהודה's. The ברייתא letting a חרש separate תרומה even from the start is רבי מאיר's, because he says hearing doesn't matter, only intention.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this (point)
You can even say
He holds (this opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: In this answer the 'from the start' ברייתא is no longer רבי יהודה's. It moves to רבי מאיר. Don't mix this up with the first answer in Step 10.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
phrases.notes: He means: now that we have quoted the whole ברייתא, including רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: you can even say
that Rabbi Yehuda holds like his teacher,
and it is still not difficult:
this one is Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: This is the ברכת המזון ברייתא: only after the fact.

phrases.english: that one is Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא letting a חרש separate תרומה even from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second solution to Step 9, made possible by רבי מאיר's view in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the sources to two different תנאים (רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first answer assumed רבי יהודה disagreed with his teacher.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher (only after the fact). The lenient 'from the start' ברייתא is רבי מאיר's.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה on both points
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא in the name of רב שילא rules like רבי יהודה's report of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and also like רבי יהודה in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רב שילא: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who spoke in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion with a practical ruling. The ruling follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view as reported by רבי יהודה: one should make שמע heard to his ears. The second ruling follows רבי יהודה's view in our משנה, as the second line refers back to it. Together they give the middle path: say it audibly from the start, but it still counts after the fact if you didn't.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows (this opinion)
An אמורא who reports this ruling
The אמורא in whose name the ruling is said

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, say קריאת שמע loud enough to hear yourself. If you said it without hearing, it still counts after the fact.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line of the whole debate about whether קריאת שמע must be heard.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said in the name of Rav Sheila:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
and the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁילָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the attributions are settled, gives the final practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: make קריאת שמע audible to your own ears from the start, but if you did not, it still counts after the fact.

steps.title: Why both of רב חסדא's rulings are needed
steps.stepSummary: Each of רב חסדא's two rulings blocks a different mistake. Together they teach: hear your words from the start, but if you did not, it still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings are needed. If he had only said 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה,' I would have thought you may even say שמע silently from the start. So he teaches that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה as he reported from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. If he had only said that, I would have thought you must hear it, and if you did not, there is no fix. So he also teaches that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why did רב חסדא need two rulings when one seems enough? Each ruling stops a different wrong conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling 'like רבי יהודה' alone could suggest saying שמע silently is fine even from the start. Ruling 'like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה' alone could suggest that failing to hear it makes the קריאת שמע invalid. Together they give the full rule: לכתחילה you must hear your words, but בדיעבד you have fulfilled the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is needed: both statements are necessary
I would have said: the mistaken first assumption
He teaches us: the point being made
From the start, the ideal way to act
He has no fix: after the fact it does not count

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה for קריאת שמע: from the start, say it loud enough to hear yourself. If you did not, you still fulfilled the מצוה.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if he had taught us that the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
I would have said: even from the start,
so he teaches us that the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.
And if he had taught us that the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא צָרִיךְ וְאֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה.
phrases.english: I would have said: he must, and he has no fix.
phrases.notes: He means that if you did not hear yourself, your קריאת שמע would not count at all.

phrases.english: So he teaches us that the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the double ruling in step 13 is not repetitive.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each statement is necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One ruling alone would give either too lenient a rule (fine from the start) or too strict a rule (invalid after the fact).
steps.terutzMaskana: From the start you must hear your words, but after the fact it counts.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For קריאת שמע, hearing your own words is required from the start but does not hold back the מצוה after the fact.

steps.title: רב יוסף limits the argument to קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the argument is only about קריאת שמע. For other מצוות, everyone agrees that if you did not hear your words, it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The argument is only about קריאת שמע. For other מצוות, everyone agrees he has not fulfilled the מצוה, as it says: 'Pay attention and hear, ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new statement about how far the argument in the משנה reaches. In this first version, other מצוות are stricter than שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He brings a פסוק that seems to require hearing in general, so he concludes that for other מצוות no one would accept words you did not hear. Only קריאת שמע, according to this version, has room for the lenient view. The next step will challenge this.

keyTerms.meaning: A disagreement between the תנאים
All other מצוות
Everyone agrees
He has not fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The disagreement is about the reading of Shema,
but with the other מצוות,
everyone agrees he has not fulfilled his obligation,
as it is written: "Pay attention and hear, Israel."
phrases.notes: דברים 27:9

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the final ruling on שמע to the question of how the rule applies to other מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First version: for all other מצוות, everyone agrees that words you did not hear do not count.

steps.title: A ברייתא about ברכת המזון challenges רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that ברכת המזון said silently counts after the fact. That contradicts רב יוסף's claim that for other מצוות it never counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: A person should not say ברכת המזון in his heart, but if he did, he has fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's statement with a ברייתא. ברכת המזון is one of the 'other מצוות,' yet it counts after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said that for other מצוות everyone agrees it does not count. This ברייתא shows a case outside of שמע where it does count after the fact. So his first version cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, usually from a ברייתא
The blessing after eating bread
In his heart: silently, without hearing himself

phrases.english: They challenged:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְבָרֵךְ אָדָם בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן בְּלִבּוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should not say Grace after Meals in his heart,
and if he did say it that way, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: לֹא יְבָרֵךְ אָדָם בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן בְּלִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב יוסף's statement from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that for other מצוות everyone agrees it does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ברכת המזון is one of the other מצוות, and the ברייתא says it counts after the fact, so not everyone holds it fails.

steps.title: רב יוסף's statement is re-stated the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes רב יוסף's words. The argument is only in שמע, because of the word 'שמע.' For other מצוות, everyone agrees it does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רב יוסף said the argument is about קריאת שמע, because it is written 'שמע ישראל.' But for other מצוות, everyone agrees he has fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the challenge by saying רב יוסף actually said the opposite. Other מצוות are more lenient than שמע, not stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict view exists only in שמע, because its פסוק uses the word 'שמע' (hear). Other מצוות have no such word, so everyone agrees that silent words count. This fits the ברייתא about ברכת המזון perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said: a corrected version of a statement
He has fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. The final version of רב יוסף makes other מצוות more lenient than שמע: silent words count there according to everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: Only קריאת שמע has an argument about hearing your own words, because of the word 'שמע.' In other מצוות, like ברכת המזון, everyone agrees it counts after the fact.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
Rav Yosef said:
The disagreement is about the reading of Shema,
as it is written: "Hear, Israel,"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: but with the other מצוות,
everyone agrees he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by changing the wording of רב יוסף's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-stating the statement (אי אתמר הכי אתמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Other מצוות are stricter than שמע: silent words never count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Other מצוות are more lenient: everyone agrees silent words count. The argument exists only in שמע, because of the word 'שמע.'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Outside קריאת שמע, saying a ברכה without hearing it still counts according to everyone.

steps.title: A verse that seems to demand hearing everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that only שמע needs hearing, pointing to the פסוק 'הסכת ושמע ישראל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'Pay attention and hear, Israel'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. It quotes a different פסוק that also uses the word 'שמע.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the argument is only about קריאת שמע, because of the word 'שמע' there. For other מצוות, everyone agrees it counts even if you did not hear. But this פסוק also says 'שמע,' so maybe hearing is needed in other areas too.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
Pay attention, be quiet and listen
And hear

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"Pay attention and hear, Israel"!
phrases.notes: דברים 27:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 17's claim that, apart from שמע, everyone agrees that not hearing your words still counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק also says 'שמע.' If the word 'שמע' means you must hear, then hearing should be needed beyond קריאת שמע too.

steps.title: That verse is about learning Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'הסכת ושמע ישראל' is about learning תורה, so it does not affect other מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about words of תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the פסוק is talking about learning תורה, not about saying a ברכה or doing a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'שמע' in this פסוק means paying close attention while learning תורה. It is not a rule that every spoken מצוה must be heard by your own ears. So Step 17 still stands: outside of קריאת שמע, everyone agrees it counts.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (that פסוק)
Words of תורה, learning תורה

steps.whatToRemember: Only in קריאת שמע is there an argument about hearing your own words. The פסוק 'הסכת ושמע' is about learning תורה carefully.

phrases.english: That verse
is written about words of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the challenging פסוק to a different topic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הסכת ושמע' teaches that every spoken מצוה must be heard.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הסכת ושמע' is about paying attention when learning תורה. It does not make other מצוות need hearing.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's case of unclear letters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of someone who read שמע without saying the letters carefully.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who read and was not careful with its letters.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It quotes a line from the משנה so it can give the הלכה about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי says this person is יוצא and רבי יהודה says he is not. Right before it, the משנה had another dispute about not hearing your own words. Quoting this line brings both disputes back into view for the ruling that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He read (here, he said קריאת שמע)
Was careful and exact
Its letters

phrases.english: "One who read and was not careful with its letters."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the hearing question to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: someone who said שמע without saying the letters clearly. רבי יוסי says he is יוצא, רבי יהודה says he is not.

steps.title: The הלכה follows the lenient side in both disputes
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבי in the name of רבי יאשיה rules that in both disputes of the משנה, we follow the lenient opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טבי said in the name of רבי יאשיה: The הלכה follows the words of both of them, to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה. In both disputes of the משנה, we follow whoever is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For not hearing your own words, the lenient one is the תנא קמא, who says it counts. For not saying the letters clearly, the lenient one is רבי יוסי, who says it counts. So in both cases, after the fact, the person is יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who reports this ruling
The אמורא in whose name the ruling is said
Both of them, both disputes
To be lenient

steps.whatToRemember: After the fact, קריאת שמע counts even if you did not hear your words (like the תנא קמא) and even if you did not say the letters clearly (like רבי יוסי).
steps.confusionAlert: 'Both of them' does not mean two people agree. It means two separate disputes, and in each one we pick the lenient side. רבי יוסי is strict in one and lenient in the other, so we follow him in only one of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for someone who said קריאת שמע quietly or without care: he does not need to say it again. Even so, Step 14 taught that you should hear your words from the start.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tavi said
that Rabbi Yoshiya said:
The halacha follows the words of both of them,
to be lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on the משנה line quoted in Step 20, together with the hearing dispute next to it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In both disputes we follow the lenient side. Not hearing your words counts (תנא קמא), and not saying the letters clearly counts (רבי יוסי).

steps.title: The grave is like a womb: it takes in and gives back
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבי, quoting רבי יאשיה, explains why a פסוק in משלי puts the grave next to the womb. Just as a womb takes in and brings out, a grave takes in and will bring out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טבי said in the name of רבי יאשיה: The פסוק says, 'Three things are never satisfied: the grave and the closed womb.' Why is a grave mentioned next to a womb? To teach that just as a womb takes in and brings out, so too a grave takes in and will bring out.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just quoted a ruling from רבי טבי in the name of רבי יאשיה, it now brings another teaching from the same pair. He explains a פסוק that puts the grave and the womb side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'what does a grave have to do with a womb?' shows that the pairing must teach something. The answer is that both take something in and later give it out. For the grave, this means the dead will one day come back out.

keyTerms.meaning: The grave, the place of the dead
Womb
Takes in and brings out
What does this have to do with that?

steps.confusionAlert: This teaching has nothing to do with קריאת שמע. The גמרא brings it only because it comes from the same רבי טבי and רבי יאשיה quoted in the last step.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Tavi said that Rabbi Yoshiya said:
What is meant by what is written:
"There are three that are never satisfied...
the grave and the closed womb."

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן שְׁאוֹל אֵצֶל רֶחֶם?
phrases.english: What does a grave have to do with a womb?
Rather, it comes to tell you:
Just as a womb takes in and brings out,
so too a grave takes in and brings out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching from the same speakers as Step 21, on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the grave is placed next to the womb, the grave also 'brings out': the dead will come back to life.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: the dead will come out with great noise
steps.stepSummary: A baby enters the womb quietly but comes out with loud cries. The dead enter the grave with loud crying, so they will surely come out with loud noise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? A womb takes in quietly, yet a baby comes out with loud cries. A grave takes in with loud crying, so surely the dead will come out with loud noise.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching builds on the comparison of grave and womb with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'lighter' case is the womb: something goes in quietly and still comes out loudly. The 'stronger' case is the grave, where the dead go in with loud mourning. So the coming-out of the dead should certainly be loud too.

keyTerms.meaning: A reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger one
Quietly, in private
With great noise, loud cries
Isn't it logical that...?

phrases.english: And is this not a kal vachomer:
If a womb, which things are put into quietly,
is still emptied with loud cries,
phrases.notes: He means the cries at birth, when the baby comes out.

phrases.english: then the grave, which people are put into with loud cries,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁמּוֹצִיאִין מִמֶּנּוּ בְּקוֹלֵי קוֹלוֹת?
phrases.english: isn't it logical that they will come out of it with loud cries?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the grave-womb comparison of Step 22 with a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: That the dead will come out of the grave with great noise
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the womb, which takes in quietly and still gives out loudly

steps.title: This answers those who deny תחיית המתים in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: From this teaching we have an answer to those who say תחיית המתים has no source in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here there is an answer to those who say that תחיית המתים is not from the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching ends by saying what it proves: there is a source in the פסוקים for תחיית המתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grave-womb comparison shows from a פסוק that the grave gives back the dead. That is a direct answer to people who claim תחיית המתים has no source in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead coming back to life
An answer, a reply against someone's claim
From the תורה, having a source in the written text

steps.whatToRemember: The grave is like a womb: what goes in will come out. This is a source for תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: From here is an answer to those who say
that resurrection of the dead is not from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States what Steps 22–23 prove.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The grave-womb teaching is a source showing that תחיית המתים comes from the פסוקים.

steps.title: 'וכתבתם': everything must be written, even the commands
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא teaches before רבא that the word 'וכתבתם' means everything must be written, even the צוואות (commands).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא taught before רבא: 'And you shall write them' teaches that everything must be in writing, even the commands.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אושעיא repeats a ברייתא to רבא about what must be written in a מזוזה (and תפילין).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from 'וכתבתם' that nothing in the פרשה is left out, not even the command lines themselves. This sets up רבא's question in the next step about who holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall write them' (the פסוק of מזוזה)
Commands, instruction lines
Taught (a ברייתא)
Before him, in front of him

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya taught before Rava:
"And you shall write them"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:9, the מזוזה פסוק.

phrases.english: everything must be in writing,
even the commands.
phrases.notes: The command lines, like 'and you shall write them,' are also written, not skipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about writing מזוזה and תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everything in the פרשה must be written, even the commands.

steps.title: רבא: this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view. He holds that in a סוטה scroll, the curses are written but the commands are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Who taught you this? It is רבי יהודה. He said about a סוטה that one writes the curses but does not write the commands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא identifies who holds this ברייתא and connects it to רבי יהודה's ruling about the סוטה scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a סוטה, רבי יהודה says only the curses are written, not the commands. Since he makes a difference between curses and commands there, it makes sense that he is the one who needs to say the commands are written in מזוזה. The next step explains why the two cases differ.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Whose view is this?
A woman suspected of being unfaithful, who is tested with written curses
Curses
Regarding, about

phrases.english: He said to him: Who said this to you?
It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who said regarding a sota:
one writes the curses, but does not write the commands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies who holds the ברייתא of Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view. He holds that a סוטה scroll has only curses, without commands.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה treats סוטה and מזוזה differently
steps.stepSummary: For סוטה, the פסוק says only 'וכתב' (and he shall write), so only the curses are written. For מזוזה, the פסוק says 'וכתבתם' (write it complete), so even the commands are written.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, by סוטה, it is written 'And he shall write these curses.' But here, where it is written 'And you shall write them,' even the commands are written too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his explanation. He shows how רבי יהודה can say 'no commands' for סוטה and 'yes commands' for מזוזה: each case follows its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא contrasts the verbs in the two פסוקים. By סוטה the פסוק says plain 'וכתב' (and he shall write), so only the curses are written. By מזוזה it says 'וכתבתם', read as 'write it complete' (תם), so even the commands are written. The next step asks whether 'וכתב' is really רבי יהודה's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the case of סוטה)
Here (the case of מזוזה)
'And he shall write these curses' (the סוטה פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה: סוטה gets only the curses ('these curses'). מזוזה and תפילין get everything, even the commands ('וכתבתם').
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the cases. 'No commands' is only for the סוטה scroll. For מזוזה and תפילין, even the commands are written.

phrases.english: And there, it is written:
"And he shall write these curses,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:23

phrases.english: but here, where it is written "And you shall write them,"
even the commands are also written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's statement from step 26, explaining why רבי יהודה, who leaves out commands for סוטה, requires them for מזוזה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different wording in the פסוקים for each case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי יהודה would leave out commands everywhere, as he does by סוטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case follows its own פסוק. Plain 'וכתב' by סוטה covers only the curses, while 'וכתבתם' (write it complete) by מזוזה includes even the commands.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's reason comes from 'curses', not from 'and he shall write'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 27. רבי יהודה's reason in סוטה is the word 'אלות' (curses), not the word 'וכתב'. So why does מזוזה need 'וכתבתם' to include the commands?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is רבי יהודה's reason really because it says 'and he shall write'? His reason is because it says 'curses': curses yes, commands no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 27. It says the contrast between 'וכתב' and 'וכתבתם' is not where רבי יהודה's rule really comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In סוטה, the commands are left out because the פסוק says 'these curses', which limits the writing to curses only. מזוזה has no limiting word like that. So everything should be written anyway, and the extra word 'וכתבתם' seems to be unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a word that opens a challenge)
his reason
curses (in the סוטה section)
commands (the instructions in the section)

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Yehuda's reason
is because it is written "and he shall write"?
phrases.notes: This is the word in the סוטה section about the כהן writing the scroll (במדבר 5:23).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda's reason
is because it is written "curses".
Curses, yes; commands, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב וְכָתַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the contrast between וכתב and וכתבתם that Step 27 used
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'וכתבתם' is needed in מזוזה to include the commands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה excludes the commands in סוטה only because of the limiting word 'אלות'. מזוזה has no such limit, so the commands would be included even without 'וכתבתם'.

steps.title: 'וכתבתם' prevents learning מזוזה from סוטה
steps.stepSummary: The word 'וכתבתם' is necessary. Without it, we might have used the shared word 'writing' to learn מזוזה from סוטה, and then left out the commands in מזוזה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. Otherwise you might think: let us learn 'writing' from 'writing' in סוטה. Just as there it is curses yes and commands no, so too here, commands no. So the תורה wrote 'וכתבתם', meaning even the commands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing why 'וכתבתם' is not extra. It blocks a comparison we might otherwise have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both סוטה and מזוזה use a word for 'writing'. That could link them through a גזירה שוה, which would carry the סוטה limit (no commands) over to מזוזה. 'וכתבתם' breaks that link and teaches that in מזוזה even the commands are written.

keyTerms.meaning: it was necessary
it would have entered your mind to say
let us learn (one case from another)
'writing' and 'writing': the shared word that links two sections
the Merciful One (the תורה)

steps.whatToRemember: In סוטה only the curses are written, because the פסוק says 'אלות'. In מזוזה even the commands are written, because 'וכתבתם' stops us from copying the סוטה rule.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
for it would have entered your mind to say
let us learn "writing" from "writing" there:
just as there
curses, yes; commands, no,
so too here also
commands, no.
So the Merciful One wrote "and you shall write them"
meaning even the commands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the word blocks a mistaken גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learn מזוזה from סוטה through the shared word 'writing', and leave out the commands
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וכתבתם' teaches that in מזוזה even the commands are written

steps.title: Your teaching must be complete: separate words that run together
steps.stepSummary: רב עובדיה teaches before רבא that 'ולמדתם' means your learning must be 'תם' (complete). You must leave a space between words that are stuck together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עובדיה taught before רבא: 'And you shall teach them' means your teaching should be complete, so one must leave space between words that are joined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about reading the words of קריאת שמע clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולמדתם' is read as 'למוד תם', complete learning. Complete learning means saying each word clearly. When one word ends with the same letter the next word begins with, you must pause so the two words don't blur into one.

keyTerms.meaning: taught (a ברייתא)
and you shall teach them
complete, whole
space, a pause
the 'stuck together' words

phrases.english: Rav Ovadya taught before Rava:
"And you shall teach them"
phrases.notes: דברים 11:19. The word is read as two parts: 'לימוד' (teaching) and 'תם' (complete).

phrases.english: means that your teaching should be complete
so that one leaves space between the joined words.
phrases.notes: These are words where one ends with the same letter the next one starts with, so they easily blur together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching that, like Step 25, derives a rule from a word in the פרשה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'ולמדתם': one must pause between words where the end of one runs into the start of the next

steps.title: רבא lists examples of joined words
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains רב עובדיה's rule by listing pairs of words in קריאת שמע that must be separated clearly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא responded after him: for example, 'על לבבך', 'על לבבכם', 'בכל לבבך', 'בכל לבבכם', 'עשב בשדך', 'ואבדתם מהרה', 'הכנף פתיל', 'אתכם מארץ'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds concrete examples to show exactly which words רב עובדיה meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each pair, the last letter of the first word matches or sounds like the first letter of the next word (ל-ל, ב-ב, ם-מ, ף-פ). Without a pause, the reader swallows one letter and changes the words. רבא does not add a new law; he defines the scope of 'הדבקים'.

keyTerms.meaning: responded, added
after him
for example

steps.whatToRemember: When saying קריאת שמע, pause between words like 'על לבבך' or 'ואבדתם מהרה' so each word is heard fully.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of carefully separating these word pairs when reading קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: Rava responded after him:
For example, "on your heart" (singular), "on your heart" (plural),
phrases.notes: In each pair, the first word ends with the same letter or sound that the next word begins with.

phrases.english: "with all your heart" (singular), "with all your heart" (plural),
"grass in your field", "and you will perish quickly",
"the corner, a thread", "you from the land".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and illustrates רב עובדיה's teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'joined words' are pairs like על לבבך and ואבדתם מהרה, where the edge letters run together

steps.title: Saying the שמע carefully cools גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that whoever says קריאת שמע and is careful with its letters has גיהנם cooled for him. He proves it by rereading two words in a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: Anyone who says קריאת שמע and is careful to say each letter correctly, גיהנם is cooled down for him. The source is the פסוק: 'When the Almighty scatters kings over it, it will snow in צלמון.' Do not read 'בפרש' with a שׂ (scatters). Read it with a שׁ (says clearly). Do not read 'בצלמון.' Read 'בצלמות' (shadow of death). So: when a person says clearly, God makes it snow in the shadow of death, which means He cools גיהנם for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the reward for saying קריאת שמע clearly and carefully. This builds on רבא's list of words that must be separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before taught the rule that you must say קריאת שמע clearly. Now רבי חמא ברבי חנינא tells us the reward for following that rule. He gets it by changing how we read two words in the פסוק: 'scatters' becomes 'says clearly,' and the place 'צלמון' becomes 'shadow of death,' meaning גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: Is careful and exact, here in saying each letter correctly
They cool down
The place where souls are punished after death
Do not read it as ... but as ... A way of drawing a new lesson from a פסוק by reading a word differently
Shadow of death, used here to mean גיהנם

steps.whatToRemember: Saying קריאת שמע clearly is more than a technical rule. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that it has a great reward: גיהנם is cooled for the person who does it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the written פסוק is wrong or should be changed. The פסוק stays as it is. The גמרא is drawing an extra lesson by reading the words in a slightly different way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the reason behind all the careful rules in the steps before. Being exact with the words of קריאת שמע carries a real spiritual reward.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
Anyone who recites the Shema
and is careful in saying its letters,
Gehinnom is cooled for him,
as it is said: 'When the Almighty scatters kings over it,
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:15

phrases.english: it will snow in Tzalmon.'
Do not read 'befares' (when He scatters), but 'befaresh' (when one says clearly),
Do not read 'beTzalmon' (in Tzalmon), but 'betzalmavet' (in the shadow of death).

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי חמא ברבי חנינא: כל הקורא קריאת שמע ומדקדק באותיותיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב עובדיה and רבא taught that קריאת שמע must be said clearly, this step adds the reward for doing so.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever says קריאת שמע carefully and clearly has גיהנם cooled for him, learned from a new reading of תהלים 68:15.

steps.title: A second teaching begins: why are passages placed next to each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins another teaching from רבי חמא ברבי חנינא, asking why certain things were placed next to each other. The teaching continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חמא ברבי חנינא also said: Why were [these] placed next to each other...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new teaching from the same רבי חמא ברבי חנינא. Here it only opens with the question 'why were they placed next to each other,' and the full teaching comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ואמר' (and he also said) tells us this is another teaching from the same person. It is often placed here because it comes from the same רבי. The question 'למה נסמכו' introduces a lesson drawn from two sections that appear side by side. What those sections are and his answer come on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: And he also said, bringing another teaching from the same person
Why were they placed next to each other? A question about why two sections sit side by side

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, also said:
Why were [these] placed next to each other...

steps.triggerLanguage: ואמר רבי חמא ברבי חנינא: למה נסמכו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This brings a second teaching from the same רבי חמא ברבי חנינא, linked by speaker rather than by topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the opening is given here: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא asks why certain sections were placed next to each other. His answer comes on the next עמוד.
